answer_1.quote: long-form table question answering (LFTQA) has emerged as a vibrant area of research, bridging the gap between structured data and the comprehensive insights required in real-world scenarios.
answer_1.outputs: paragraph-length answers generated from tabular data

answer_2.quote: We examine following automatic metrics that are widely used in the LFTQA task, investigating their reliability in evaluating model performance: • BLEU ... • ROUGE ... • METEOR ... • BERTScore ... • TAPAS-Acc ... • AutoACU ... We also adopt an LLM-based evaluation system, G-Eval ...

answer_3.quote: We also adopt an LLM-based evaluation system, G-Eval ... G-Eval employs LLMs using a chain-of-thought approach and the form-filling paradigm to assess the quality of generated text.

answer_4.quote: We tasked annotators to evaluate answers using a Likert scale ranging from 1 to 5 for the criteria of faithfulness and comprehensiveness, individually.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated faithfulness (rooted in source table, correct information, no hallucinations) and comprehensiveness (include all relevant information addressing the user's question).
